title: Sugar Importer With Trump Ties Said to Maintain Abusive Labor Practices
partialText: A watchdog group said the Dominican company continued to violate labor standards after President Trump lifted an import ban last year.

title: An A.I. Tax Boom Could Curtail America’s Debt. But Not Solve It.
partialText: The consequences of A.I. for the budget will largely hinge on whether — and to what extent — the technology reshapes the labor market.

title: Gulf Oil Giants Push to Expand Overseas Stockpiles as Iran War Drags On
partialText: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are seeking larger oil reserves in Japan and South Korea as regional conflict threatens supply routes.

title: Home Depot Reports Higher Sales, but Its C.E.O. Isn’t There to Spread the News
partialText: Investors got a shock last week when the retailer said that Ted Decker, the chief executive, would take a medical leave. Tuesday’s earnings brought a more welcome surprise.

title: ABC Sues Trump Administration Over F.C.C. Threat to Its TV Licenses
partialText: The network asked a court to stop the agency from taking steps that could force ABC stations off the air and accused the F.C.C. of violating its First Amendment rights.

title: Ship Exiting the Strait of Hormuz Is Attacked
partialText: At least 17 commercial sailors have been killed in and around Iranian and Omani waters since March. Six months into the conflict, the vital waterway remains exceptionally dangerous.

title: Is Silicon Valley in the Justice Dept.’s Sights?
partialText: Federal prosecutors are reportedly investigating Andreessen Horowitz, the venture capital giant, over board seats it holds.

title: Bond Yields Jump and Stocks Slip as Iran Stalemate Unsettles Investors
partialText: The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond rose to its highest level in nearly 20 years.

title: At Ex-Premier Zhu Rongji’s Funeral, China’s Past Shadows Its Present
partialText: Beijing wants to portray today’s China as carrying forward Zhu Rongji’s era of growth, but for many Chinese, the optimism of that time has since faded.

title: What’s in an Airport Code? In West Palm Beach, It’s the President’s Initials.
partialText: The state’s Palm Beach International Airport has been renamed for the president, complete with a rare change in its three-letter airport code.

title: It’s Crunchtime Again for Canada to Avoid Trump’s New Tariffs
partialText: Canada is seeking a deal to dodge further economic pain at the hands of the Trump administration on midnight Tuesday. But at what cost?

title: India’s College Boom Is Leaving Graduates in Debt and Without Jobs
partialText: Families are betting their savings on private universities as a path to a better life. A shortage of well-paying work is turning that wager into frustration.

title: Paramount Asks States to Shoulder Costs of Delaying Warner Bros. Deal
partialText: Paramount’s $111 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery has been postponed until the conclusion of a trial, a delay the studio says could cost it millions of dollars.

title: ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’ Lenders Pitch Loans for Needs Like Electricity and Rent
partialText: The rapid growth of pay-later loans raises questions about whether their popularity is driven by consumer preference or desperation.

title: Mark Cuban and Other Founders Wade Into Wealth Tax Debate
partialText: Some entrepreneurs, including Mark Cuban, are publicly worried about the potential fallout from California’s proposal to impose a special billionaire tax.

title: A French Start-Up, Inbolt, Makes Robots See, and Work, Better
partialText: Inbolt, a French start-up that sells robot vision systems, helped a Stellantis plant in Detroit become a top performer in the company.

title: As China Hunts for Scientific Talent, the US Makes It Easier
partialText: Young researchers have long come to the U.S. for academic training, but a combination of Chinese money and U.S. restrictions is shifting the balance.

title: Should I Publicize a Bad Publicist?
partialText: Plus: An intern considers whether to give the boss an honest review.

title: How a False Nuclear Claim About Iran Ricocheted From India to Washington
partialText: A dubious post that spread on X became the basis of false claims that Iran’s leadership had declared it a nuclear power.

title: As A.I. Data Centers Spread, Pressure Mounts to Share Profits
partialText: Policymakers around the country are maneuvering to ensure that tech giants aren’t the only ones who stand to benefit.

title: 2 Planes With Same Call Sign in Phoenix Could Have Been ‘Disastrous’
partialText: An air traffic controller noticed that two planes — one departing, one landing — were both flight 2482. He acted quickly to avoid confusion.

title: The Cutthroat Wearables Battle Is About More Than Tracking Your Fitness
partialText: Google, Apple, Samsung and upstarts like Oura are racing to integrate data from their wearable devices into the health care system.

title: Sports Team Sale Prices Keep Hitting New Highs
partialText: The deal for the Los Angeles Lakers valued the team at a record $12.5 billion, eclipsing the $10 billion paid for the franchise just last year.

title: Worker Pay Isn’t Keeping Up With Inflation Once Again
partialText: When prices spiked in 2021-22, wages failed to keep up for many workers, new research shows. Now the pattern is repeating.

title: How to Protect Your Home While You’re on Vacation
partialText: Store food in sealed containers and fix any leaking faucets or pipes, experts told our columnist, who had her own nightmare upon returning home.

title: How Cyclospora Evaded the U.S. Food Safety System to Sicken Thousands
partialText: The Trump administration delayed a rule last year that could have sped up the effort to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Critics charge that food safety oversight has eroded overall.

title: FDA Classifies Egg Recall as Class I for Highest Health Risk
partialText: Nearly 20 million eggs were recalled in July over salmonella concerns. The new classification signals a “reasonable probability” of “serious adverse health consequences or death.”

title: Hiroshi Okuda, Disrupter Who Revived Toyota in the 1990s, Dies at 93
partialText: As the car company’s president, he made decisions quickly and shook things up, expanding overseas manufacturing and introducing the Prius, a milestone in automotive history.

title: Lawsuit Accuses Selena Gomez of Defrauding Investors in Mental Health Site
partialText: The actor, singer and beauty mogul founded Wondermind, a mental health platform, with her mother. Investors put in more than $1 million in the venture, which “quietly collapsed,” the suit said.

title: Google Turns On Gemini A.I. for Students Using Its Classroom App
partialText: Google enabled A.I. features for K-12 schools that have allowed student access to Gemini. Until this week, Google automatically enabled Gemini in Classroom only for students 18 or older.

title: Outrage at UnitedHealth and Other Insurers Persists After Brian Thompson Killing
partialText: Higher premiums and rising medical bills have intensified Americans’ dissatisfaction with their medical coverage.

title: Jeff Bezos Buys a Piece of Liverpool Football Club
partialText: It is the first known investment by Mr. Bezos, one of the world’s richest men, into a sports team.

title: July Retail Sales Notch Biggest Drop in Over a Year
partialText: The data for July showed the biggest drop in more than a year, as American households face the economic strains brought on by persistent inflation

title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
partialText: Investment gains at Alphabet and Amazon reveal a new way in which technology companies’ fortunes are increasingly linked.

title: Why Japan Is Struggling to Stop the Yen’s Decline
partialText: The currency has resumed its slide, eroding gains after the U.S. Treasury intervened to prop it up, as concerns mount about the direction of the country’s spending.

title: The Markets Have Been on a Roll. Is It Time to Hedge Your Bets?
partialText: The S&P 500 is in position for a rare fourth year of consecutive double-digit gains. Risks are rising, our columnist says, yet Wall Street is doubling down.

title: Robinhood Bets Again on a Public Venture Capital Fund
partialText: The trading platform raised $200 million for a second publicly traded vehicle to let ordinary investors buy into privately held start-ups.

title: New Yorkers Can’t Stop Lining Up for This Sushi
partialText: At a proliferating number of stores, discounts on sushi and other items are offered after 8 p.m. To get the best meals, you have to be there early.

title: A Silicon Valley Dirt Farmer Hangs Up His Shears
partialText: Andy Mariani grows exotic and ethereally delicious stone fruit in the shadow of tech giants. But at age 80, it’s time to give up the land.

title: How Pennsylvania Got Hooked on Games That Look a Lot Like Slot Machines
partialText: A legal loophole kept “skill games” from being considered gambling. Now lawmakers are trying to save them from a court ruling.

title: Kalshi Ordered to Cease Most Operations in Washington State
partialText: In a preliminary injunction, a state judge barred the prediction market from allowing residents to place bets on the bulk of its offerings.

title: Salvage Company Hoping to Sell Titanic Artifacts Challenges Court’s Role
partialText: A Virginia federal court has awarded the company the rights to collect, but not sell, items from the shipwreck. But the company says its earliest retrievals are governed by a French court.

title: Flock Announces Privacy Updates to Its Car-Tracking Cameras
partialText: Critics say the measures are “public relations” and leave room for continued misuse.

title: Alfonso Fanjul Jr., Cuban American Sugar Baron, Dies at 89
partialText: With his brother, he presided over a family empire that includes the world’s largest cane sugar refiner and the Domino and C&H brands.

title: In a Chinese Leader’s Death, Mourning for a More Hopeful Time
partialText: Tributes for former Premier Zhu Rongji reflect nostalgia for an era when China was opening to the world and the future seemed more prosperous and hopeful.

title: How Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner’s Bromance Led Them to Lakers
partialText: Bob Iger, the former chief executive of Disney, and Josh Kushner, the venture capitalist, are buying the Los Angeles Lakers. Their wives set them up.

title: Inside the $12.5 Billion Deal for the Lakers
partialText: The transaction, hashed out last weekend, reflects the huge profit potential of major sports franchises.

title: What We Know About Taylor Farms’ Food Recalls
partialText: Just weeks after the company recalled lettuce and other produce suspected of being tainted by the cyclosporiasis parasite, it recalled jalapeños linked to a salmonella outbreak.

title: America Wants to Make Its Own Humanoid Robots. That Won’t Be Easy.
partialText: China already manufactures humanoid robots by the thousands. A new generation of U.S. start-ups is betting that there is still time to compete.

title: The Golden Age of Mexican Food Is Here. And It’s Complicated.
partialText: Even at a time of anti-immigration politics, there has never been a richer variety of Mexican restaurants in the United States.
